Nearest checks: Google Research wearable-biomarker tool vs published GlucoFM (2026-08-30) — different paper, different framework, kept as distinct; Google Research fruit-fly connectome vs published MAPL-EMIT methane (2026-09-02) — same outlet, unrelated topics, kept. Diversity guard: 5 distinct outlets, no outlet used twice, 5 distinct sub-fields (weather/climate, connectomics, experimental physics, behavioral-science method, clinical AI regulation). items.title: Introducing WeatherNext 3, our most advanced and accurate global weather AI model
items.excerpt: DeepMind's new global weather model claims its most accurate forecasts yet, extending the run of AI systems that outperform physics-based numerical weather prediction at a fraction of the compute.
items.rationale: The flagship AI weather model gets another generation, and each one further displaces physics-based NWP as the operational default for forecasting.

items.title: A connectomics milestone: Mapping the complete male fruit fly brain
items.excerpt: Google Research and collaborators completed a full synapse-level map of the male fruit fly brain, an AI-segmentation feat over petabytes of electron microscopy that gives neuroscience a second complete connectome to compare against.
items.rationale: A second complete connectome turns single-specimen anatomy into comparative neuroscience, and it exists only because AI segmentation can now handle petabyte-scale microscopy.

items.title: AI suggests new physics experiments that could outperform human-designed setups
items.excerpt: Researchers report an AI system that proposes experimental setups for probing the laws of nature, generating designs that beat human-devised configurations. It shifts AI from analyzing results to authoring the experiment itself.
items.rationale: AI moves upstream from analyzing data to designing the apparatus, and the machine-authored setups reportedly beat what physicists devised themselves.

items.title: AI agents aren't ready to replace humans in behavioral research
items.excerpt: New work tests whether LLM 'silicon subjects' can stand in for human participants in behavioral studies, and finds the simulated populations diverge from real ones in ways that would corrupt findings.
items.rationale: A direct, method-changing verdict on 'silicon subjects' — anyone tempted to run studies on synthetic participants now has measured failure modes to answer for.

items.title: FDA pilot offers generative AI medical devices a path to patients before they are authorized
items.excerpt: The FDA's new pilot would let generative-AI medical devices reach patients ahead of full authorization, a regulatory experiment that changes how fast clinical AI can move from lab to bedside.
items.rationale: The regulatory gate, not the model, has been the bottleneck for clinical generative AI — an FDA pre-authorization path resets timelines for every group building one.
